notes:
Summary: CodeFlow Labs builds an IDE-first AI assistant for enterprise dev teams (code completion, contextual refactors, repo search). They're evaluating Redwood to replace a brittle mix of OpenAI-hosted endpoints + a self-hosted FAISS index. Key theme: repository-aware context retrieval with strict residency and low-latency streaming for in-IDE UX.

Requirements / priorities (engineer snippets):
- Latency: first-token stream target <=150ms for small completions; interactive completions must feel instant in VS Code.
- Throughput: concurrency for ~200 active editors during peak; typical per-editor request size small (128-512 tokens) but embeddings updates frequent.
- Repo-aware retrieval: incremental embedding pipeline (commit-hook or nightly), chunking by logical file boundaries, repo metadata signals (language, path, last-modified) used to bias retrieval.
- Vector DB: evaluating managed Redis/Pinecone vs on-prem Milvus/FAISS; must support sharding across AZs and fast ANN queries (<20ms p99) for top-20 matches.
- Chunking: want heuristics that keep function/cls context intact (200-600 token chunks) and store overlap for continuity. Need tooling to re-chunk on language-specific parsing.
- Residency & compliance: EU customer subset requires data and embeddings stored in EU only; cannot have embeddings mirrored to non-EU. Encryption-at-rest with customer-managed KMS mandatory.
- Model/version pinning: must pin model revisions for canary rollouts, be able to route specific teams to model variants (quantized vs fp16) and fallback to smaller model on resource pressure.
- Cost sensitivity: embedding refresh cost is material; they want Optimize suggestions (sampling policies, cache TTL, delta embeddings) to cut annualized costs.

Quote from Head of ML Eng (paraphrased): "If embedding updates can be incremental and we can serve ANN queries at <20ms, the in-editor experience becomes viable. We can't tolerate noisy global indexing or cross-region replicas for EU repos."

Technical questions raised in calls:
- How does Redwood handle incremental embedding pipelines? Can we ship commit-level deltas and avoid re-embedding entire repo?
- Can Dedicated/Private host the vector DB on premises in an air-gapped mode for select customers?
- What are observed p99 latencies for streaming first token at 8k-context models with batch sizes tuned for low latency?
- How are KV cache and prefix caching applied to code completions to reduce per-token compute?

POC scope proposal (from AE):
- 2-week pilot on Redwood Dedicated: index 50 active repos (~150k files), set up incremental embedding job, measure ANN p50/p99 and streaming first-token latency.
- Implement model pinning for two teams and test rollback behavior under induced load.
- Run cost runbook with Optimize recommendations to estimate annual embedding refresh cost.
